Approximate leave-one-out cross-validation of a fit

Source: R/loo.R
loo.stareal_fit.Rd

Estimates how well the model predicts each observed cell when that cell is left out, from the one fit: no refits. Each observed cell's own latent value is integrated out exactly before Pareto-smoothed importance sampling (PSIS; Vehtari et al. 2016, 2017), which makes the approximation stable where plain PSIS-LOO on this model is not. The result is a loo object, so loo::loo_compare() and the loo package's other tools work on it; compare_models() puts several fits side by side.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'stareal_fit'
loo(x, n_draws = NULL, verbose = FALSE, ...)

Arguments

x

A fit_areal() object.

n_draws

Number of stored draws to use, taken evenly from every chain (default: all).

verbose

Report progress.

...

Not used.

Value

A psis_loo object from the loo package (see loo::loo()), with class stareal_loo added and an extra table cells: one row per observed cell, with cell_id, id, t, time, y, k, elpd_loo (its log predictive density when left out) and pareto_k.

Details

The unit left out is an observed cell (all the surveys of one area and time step), predicted as a new survey of the cell would be, nugget included, as in crossval(). Leaving one cell out keeps its neighbours in, so this measures how well the model fills gaps between data; it says little about extrapolation to areas with no data. For that, use crossval() with folds by area or region.

Cells with a high Pareto \(\hat k\) (above 0.7, or less with fewer than about 2,200 draws: the loo package's threshold \(\min(1 - 1/\log_{10} S, 0.7)\) for \(S\) draws) have unreliable estimates; the print-out counts them. A few are normal for cells far from the rest of the data, or with very large samples. If there are many, check against crossval(), or use more draws.

References

Vehtari, A., Mononen, T., Tolvanen, V., Sivula, T. and Winther, O. (2016). Bayesian leave-one-out cross-validation approximations for Gaussian latent variable models. Journal of Machine Learning Research 17(103), 1-38.

Vehtari, A., Gelman, A. and Gabry, J. (2017). Practical Bayesian model evaluation using leave-one-out cross-validation and WAIC. Statistics and Computing 27, 1413-1432.

Examples

sim <- simulate_areal(areal_lattice(4, 4), time_frame(n_steps = 5), n_cells = 40, seed = 1)
fit <- fit_areal(sim, control = list(n_iter = 200, n_burn = 100, n_store = 50, n_chains = 2, n_cores = 1,
                                     verbose = FALSE))
loo(fit)
#> <stareal_loo> integrated PSIS-LOO over 40 observed cells, 100 draws
#>   elpd_loo -126.2 (se 4.0); p_loo 4.2; 8 cells with Pareto k > 0.50
